c.tagline: China's thousand-year Porcelain Capital, where the kilns still glow.

taxi.fareNote: Meters start around ¥8 for the first 2 km; ride-hailing via Didi is common and cheap. Few drivers speak English, so have your destination written in Chinese.

emergency.note: 110 police, 120 ambulance, 119 fire. English is rarely spoken—keep your location written in Chinese characters.

hood_landmark.Ancient Kiln & Folk Village: Ancient Kiln Folk Customs Museum Jingdezhen

hood_desc: The historic heart of the Porcelain Capital around the Imperial Kiln Museum, Zhushan (Pearl Hill), and the old ceramic workshops; the most convenient walkable base, with markets, street food, and porcelain shops at every turn.

A regenerated ceramics-factory complex turned buzzing cultural quarter, with galleries, design studios, cafes, craft-beer bars, and a lively weekend creative market—Jingdezhen's trendiest, most international area.

A green valley just south of town lined with independent ceramic studios, artist residencies, boutique guesthouses, and farm-to-table cafes; a tranquil, bohemian retreat popular with the young 'Jingpiao' artists who flock here.

Home to the 5A-rated Ancient Kiln Folk Customs Museum, where wood-fired dragon kilns and traditional porcelain-making are demonstrated live; a leafy, attraction-focused area good for a heritage-centred stay.

The modern administrative and residential side of the city across the Chang River, with newer hotels, malls, and wide avenues; quieter and less touristy, suited to travelers wanting contemporary comforts.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as locals do.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:30 PM; after that taxis and Didi fill the gap.
transit.note: Jingdezhen has no metro or tram; a network of around 20 public bus lines plus plentiful taxis and Didi ride-hailing cover the city.
transit.pay: Buses are a flat ¥1-2 paid in cash (exact change) or by mobile QR (Alipay/WeChat); there is no tourist transit card. Taxis start at about ¥8.

bus: Intercity coaches from Jingdezhen Bus Terminal

car.idp: Not recognized — China requires a Chinese driving permit

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to city center (~30 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in China and may even be refused; there is no service charge at most restaurants.
